subject: MedSprint — Billing cadence, PO field requirements & discount qualification
messages:
From: Patricia Lang <patricia.lang@medsprint.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@medsprint.health>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence, PO fields and discount qualification for upcoming engagement

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and observability features. Procurement has a few mandatory requirements we need to confirm before we can push the PO through our ERP. Key asks: 

- PO must include a Cost Center and BU code in the header (our ERP rejects otherwise). We use a 6-digit BU code (e.g., 210123).
- We need Net60 payment terms across corporate vendors unless an advance or prepay is arranged.
- Invoice cadence: our AP team prefers monthly itemized invoices per BU rather than consolidated quarterly invoices.

Linked to that: your pricing sheet shows a 15% commit discount for annual prepay and smaller banded discounts for monthly billing. Can you confirm whether: 

1) MedSprint can split invoices monthly by BU and still receive a volume-based discount?
2) Is there a way to get discount eligibility without full annual prepayment (we cannot prepay at enterprise level due to internal policy)?

Attaching our standard PO template for reference. If we can align on PO header fields and discount criteria I can route this to legal and finance.

Thanks,
Patricia Lang
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedSprint Health
Attachments: MedSprint_PO_Template_v3.xlsx
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Lang <patricia.lang@medsprint.health>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@medsprint.health>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence, PO fields and discount qualification for upcoming engagement

Hi Patricia — really appreciate the clear summary and the template. Short answers up front: yes on PO header mapping; yes to a path for discount without full annual prepay (we can do a commit + monthly invoicing structure). More detail below and next steps.

What we can support today:
- PO headers: we can map and persist a custom field for Cost Center and the 6-digit BU code. Our billing system will include those in the invoice header so your ERP can match.
- Net terms: standard is Net45 for committed volumes. We understand your policy defaults to Net60; we can accept Net60 if the contract includes a 20% smaller commit (or we can keep Net45 with a 3% early-payment incentive).
- Invoice cadence & discounting: we can issue monthly, BU-specific invoices. Discount eligibility can be structured as a "commitment ladder":
  * Commit to a 9–12 month minimum consumption that approximates the annual spend band -> qualify for the mid-tier discount (8–12%).
  * If you cannot prepay, a 30% advance on the first invoice plus the commitment gets you full mid-tier discount; otherwise we offer a slightly reduced band for pure monthly billing with no advance.

Proposed quick options (pick one):
A) Commit + 30% advance on first invoice -> Net45, mid-tier discount (10%). Monthly BU invoices, PO header mapping in place.
B) Pure monthly invoicing, no advance -> Net60, lower discount (6%), BU-specific invoices.
C) Annual prepay (if legal/policy allows for a carveout) -> Net30, top-tier discount (15%).

Next steps I suggest: Vanessa (cc'd) will confirm commercial impact and prepare an amendment draft reflecting option A or B. If you can confirm which option procurement prefers and whether the PO template in the attachment is final, I'll circulate a one-page amendment + updated invoice sample.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Account Operations, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0149
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: MedSprint — Billing cadence, PO fields and discount qualification for upcoming engagement

Irene / Vivek — quick internal:

I checked margin impact based on Patricia's asks. Two practical approaches that keep the deal moving while protecting economics: 

1) Accept option B (Pure monthly / Net60 / 6% discount) as-is for a pilot (first 3 months), then re-evaluate discount uplift once consumption stabilizes. We will need a contractual clause that allows us to reprice with 30 days' notice if usage is materially below projected committed band.

2) Prefer option A commercially (commit + 30% advance -> Net45 -> 10% mid-tier discount). For procurement we can bake in a credit mechanism: the 30% advance is applied to the first two invoices, and we include an SLA credit buffer in the amendment to address risk. This preserves cashflow but reduces collections risk.

If legal is comfortable with the reprice clause and the advance-credit flow, option A gets us closer to target ACV. If not, start with option B pilot and keep an acceleration clause.

Vivek — can you confirm internal approval for the advance-credit approach and any minimum commit floor you want (I suggest $125k ARR as a floor for the mid-tier).

Thanks,
Vanessa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks workable. Procurement is comfortable with option A if Redwood can: 
- Map Cost Center and BU header exactly as in the attached template (we will mark fields required).
- Apply the 30% advance to the first two monthly invoices as credit.
- Include a reprice trigger that allows MedSprint to pause discounts if actual monthly usage drops >35% below committed baseline (with 30 days notice).

Can you send the one-page amendment and updated invoice sample (BU line items) so I can attach both to our PO and route to Legal? Also please send DocuSign for the amendment when it's ready — legal prefers an e-sign path.

I'll get the PO prepared once I have the amendment. Appreciate the flexibility.
